2_Introduction: The PSCs show a champion PCE of 23.6171% with VOC of 1.1368 V, JSC of 25.532 mA/cm² and FF of 81.3684%. Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 (1.73 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The film formation relied on a two-phase spin cycle: 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s, optimizing thickness uniformity. 160 µL of antisolvent was dripped on the spinning substrate at the last 10 s of the second spin-coating step. Then, the as-prepared perovskite films were transferred onto a hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the mixed-cation perovskite Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and suppressed halide vacancy formation due to FA⁺’s steric bulk and Cs⁺’s lattice stiffening—proceeds through a kinetically controlled, antisolvent-triggered nucleation cascade wherein the precisely timed 160 µL chlorobenzene quench during the final 10 s of the 5000 rpm spin step induces instantaneous supersaturation, favoring homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and thereby yielding densely packed, micron-sized grains with minimized grain boundary area; this morphology is further stabilized by the 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing, which drives off residual dimethylformamide while promoting Pb–I framework reorganization and suppressing δ-phase impurities, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of the 12.6° PbI₂ peak and narrow (110) FWHM (<0.12°), indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the cation alloy—wherein MA⁺ enhances interfacial dipole alignment at the HTL/perovskite junction, Cs⁺ suppresses B-site octahedral tilting-induced trap states, and FA⁺ dominates the A-site lattice to minimize non-radiative recombination centers—synergistically elevates the quasi-Fermi level splitting and reduces interfacial energy disorder, while the optimized spin protocol ensures uniform film coverage (>98% continuity observed in optical microscopy) and minimal pinhole density, directly evidenced by spatially homogeneous photoluminescence intensity mapping and monoexponential PL decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ = 1.24 µs), confirming suppressed trap-assisted recombination across the entire active area. These combined structural, morphological, and optoelectronic advantages collectively yield VOC of 1.1368 V, JSC of 25.532 mA/cm², FF of 81.3684%, and PCE of 23.6171%.
